task.description:
PROVENANCE NOTE (read first): this run's branch feature/WF03-GH591-20260809 already existed on the remote with real prior work when ORCH claimed GH-591 via gh_claim.py -- a design artefact (src/design/iss0624-gh591-lua-11-13-fix.md, 524 lines) plus COMPLETED Step 2 (CODE-DESIGNER) and Step 2b (CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR PASS) handoffs were already present, imported from a stash by an earlier session (commit 4d5bb81, same git author identity, ~7 minutes before this claim). ORCH independently re-verified the design's soundness before trusting it (re-ran lint_design_artefact.py: exit 0; confirmed ExecutionContext genuinely lacks trace_id/pending_writes/structured_logger/instance_state today; confirmed read_variable.zig/write_variable.zig's own header comments genuinely say 'does NOT implement it'; read the instance_state dummy-singleton design in section 4.4-4.5 and confirmed its safety reasoning is sound, not hand-wavy). Registry shows a COMPLETED Step 01 (ISSUE-FIXER) entry but that handoff's JSON file itself was not included in the stash import -- a minor bookkeeping gap, not a blocker; ISS-0624.json (already filed during GH-495's run) contains the original full diagnosis this design was built from.

Implement the APPROVED design at src/design/iss0624-gh591-lua-11-13-fix.md exactly. Per Step 2b's own recorded next_action: 5 production files (executor.zig -- 4 new ExecutionContext fields: trace_id, pending_writes, structured_logger, instance_state, plus the new InstanceState struct and dummy_instance_state singleton; host_api/read_variable.zig; host_api/write_variable.zig; host_api/log.zig; structured_logger.zig if any caller-side change is needed) plus a new test file src/lua/iss0624_lua_11_13_test.zig (21 cases per the design's section 12 traceability table: 12 LUA-11 cases mapping to lua-integration.md section 16.4's 6 named tests, 9 LUA-13 cases mapping to section 18.3's 4 named tests). Wire the new test file into src/lua_test_root.zig.

Read the FULL design (524 lines) before starting -- section 3 (data flow), section 4 (the atomic apply/discard mechanics, the instance_state dummy-singleton pattern and its exact safety reasoning), section 5 (error taxonomy, especially 5.2's fail-open logging-without-a-logger decision and 5.3's null-pending_writes handling) are all load-bearing. Follow the LUA-10 active_watchdog local-copy-and-pointer-install precedent the design explicitly cites for CTX-1..CTX-4 lifetime compliance.

MANDATORY mutation testing per this session's established discipline: for at least the atomic-apply-on-success and discard-on-failure behaviors (LUA-11's core correctness claim), perform a genuine hands-on mutation test yourself -- e.g. temporarily break the commit-on-success merge logic, confirm the relevant test genuinely fails, restore the exact original code, confirm clean rebuild and passing test again. Do not skip this.
acceptance_criteria: ExecutionContext gains trace_id, pending_writes, structured_logger, instance_state fields per design section 2/4.4, all backward-compatible defaults
read_variable/write_variable genuinely read/write via pending_writes + instance_state per design section 3.1
Atomic apply-on-success / discard-on-failure implemented in executeSource per design section 4
log.zig genuinely calls structured_logger.log() with a real StructuredLogEntry per design section 3.2
New test file with 21 cases per design section 12 traceability table
Mutation test performed by hand for the atomic apply/discard behavior
zig build, zig build test-lua exit 0
No error set output from zig build

result.summary: Implemented the approved LUA-11/LUA-13 design (ISS-0624/GH-591) exactly: ExecutionContext gained trace_id/pending_writes/structured_logger/instance_state (backward-compatible defaults) plus the InstanceState struct and dummy_instance_state singleton per design section 4.5; executeSource now stages writes per-execution and atomically merges into instance_state.variables on lua_pcall success or discards (frees) them on failure; read_variable/write_variable/log.zig bodies are real per design section 3; structured_logger.zig gained a Writer injection point for test capture. Added src/lua/iss0624_lua_11_13_test.zig with 21 cases (12 LUA-11, 9 LUA-13) per design section 12's traceability table, wired into src/lua_test_root.zig. Also fixed two pre-existing test fixtures (execution_test.zig, capability_enforcement_test.zig) whose runWithGrants helpers left instance_state at the shared dummy singleton default -- writes committed there survived past their own test's boundary and corrupted a later test's freshly-reset std.testing.allocator instance when eventually freed (a genuine DebugAllocator bucket-ownership crash, reproducible and unrelated to any of my new code paths individually but triggered by wiring pending_writes into executeSource unconditionally). Also fixed a pre-existing, unrelated flaky test (limiter_wiring_test.zig TC-LUA-10-03) whose tight-loop iteration count was too small for LuaJIT's trace compiler on this hardware to reliably exceed its 1s watchdog deadline -- reproduced failing identically against unmodified main before touching it, confirming it was pre-existing and not a regression, then fixed per Unblock-Everything since it blocked a green zig build test-lua.
result.mutation_test: Performed by hand for the atomic apply-on-success / discard-on-failure behavior (LUA-11's core correctness claim): temporarily forced the commit-on-success loop in executor.zig's executeSource to always discard (deinit + free) instead of merging into instance_state.variables, rebuilt (zig build exit 0), ran zig build test-lua, and confirmed 5 tests genuinely failed as expected -- TC-ISS-0624-LUA-11-01, 06, 07, 08, 10, i.e. every test that asserts a committed value after a successful execution. TC-11-04/05 (discard-on-failure) correctly remained passing since the mutation did not touch the failure path. Restored the exact original code, confirmed a clean rebuild and 112/112 passing tests again, and reran zig build test-lua two more times to confirm stability.
result.build_verification: zig build: exit 0, no 'error set' output in stderr (grep -i 'error set' produced zero matches). zig build test-lua: 16/16 build steps succeeded, 112/112 tests passed, confirmed stable across 3 consecutive runs.
result.next_action: Route to TEST-DESIGNER / TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (Step 4) or as ORCH directs per the WF-03 pipeline
